description: A typed connection to an outside system: settings here, the credentials in the secret store.

spec.description:
A typed connection to a system outside the platform: non-secret settings here, the secret
fields in the secret store (decision D23). No value of a secret is ever part of this resource.

ownerGroup.description: Scope `group`: the Keycloak group whose members manage and use the connection.

refreshInterval.description: How often the synced Secret is refreshed from the store, for example `15m`. Between one minute and 24 hours.

scope.description:
Whose credential a connection holds and who may use it (decision D27,
internal note `design/secrets-and-connections.md` §8). Personal connections have no
resource: they live only in the secret store and never reach a pipeline.

secret.description: Where the secret part of a connection lives.

keys.description:
Names of the secret fields, for example `user` and `password`. They become the keys of the
synced Kubernetes Secret and the environment variables `CONN_<NAME>_<KEY>`.

remoteRef.description:
Path in the secret store. Absent: derived from the scope, `connections/group/<ownerGroup>/<name>`
or `connections/managed/<name>`. Set it only when the platform reads the customer's own store
(`spec.secrets` mode `external`); in platform mode the controller refuses a value, because
a path chosen by the author could point at another group's secret.

type.description: What a connection reaches. The type decides which settings and secret keys are required.

usableBy.description: Scope `managed`: the groups whose platform-run work may use the connection.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: a group connection needs ownerGroup and no usableBy
a managed connection needs usableBy and no ownerGroup
usableBy must list group names (letters, digits, dot, underscore, dash)
secret.keys must be unique names of letters, digits and underscore
config holds settings, not secrets: a name like password, secret or token belongs in secret.keys
a database connection needs config.host and the secret keys user and password
x-kubernetes-validations.rule: !(self.type in ['postgresql', 'mysql', 'sqlserver', 'oracle']) || (has(self.config) && 'host' in self.config && 'user' in self.secret.keys && 'password' in self.secret.keys)

x-kubernetes-validations.message: a rest-api connection needs config.baseUrl and the secret key token, or clientId and clientSecret
x-kubernetes-validations.rule: self.type != 'rest-api' || (has(self.config) && 'baseUrl' in self.config && ('token' in self.secret.keys || ('clientId' in self.secret.keys && 'clientSecret' in self.secret.keys)))

x-kubernetes-validations.message: an s3 connection needs config.bucket and the secret keys accessKeyId and secretAccessKey
x-kubernetes-validations.rule: self.type != 's3' || (has(self.config) && 'bucket' in self.config && 'accessKeyId' in self.secret.keys && 'secretAccessKey' in self.secret.keys)

x-kubernetes-validations.message: an sftp connection needs config.host and the secret keys user and password or privateKey
x-kubernetes-validations.rule: self.type != 'sftp' || (has(self.config) && 'host' in self.config && 'user' in self.secret.keys && ('password' in self.secret.keys || 'privateKey' in self.secret.keys))

lastSync.description: RFC 3339 time of the last successful sync from the store.

ready.description: True when the Secret exists and holds every key in `spec.secret.keys`.
